flagship.headline: The Beatles ask the cheap seats to clap and the rich to rattle their jewellery
flagship.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Royal Variety Performance at the Prince of Wales Theatre in London on November 4, 1963, with the Queen Mother and Princess Margaret in the audience, per the Beatles Bible.
flagship.summary_line_2: Before Twist and Shout, John Lennon asked the cheaper seats to clap and the rest of the house to rattle their jewellery, and the clip below is the studio Twist and Shout.

events.headline: Cream play Providence on the last night of their US farewell tour
events.summary_line_1: Cream played two shows at the Rhode Island Auditorium in Providence on November 4, 1968, the final stop of their farewell US tour, per the Rhode Island rock archive.
events.summary_line_2: The second show was cut short by a noise curfew, and the clip below is White Room, which was in the set.

events.headline: The Beatles record 12-Bar Original at Abbey Road
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles recorded the instrumental 12-Bar Original at EMI Studios on November 4, 1965, in the early hours after finishing What Goes On, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their first instrumental since signing with EMI in 1962 and stayed unreleased until Anthology 2 in 1996, and the clip below is the edited take 2 from that album.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play two shows at the New Haven Arena
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones played two shows at the New Haven Arena in Connecticut on November 4, 1965, a stop on their second American tour, per Rolling Stones Data.
events.summary_line_2: The clip below is Get Off of My Cloud, their chart-topping single that autumn.

events.headline: The Beatles play two shows at the Ritz in Luton
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two shows at the Ritz Cinema on Gordon Street in Luton on November 4, 1964, at 6.30pm and 8.45pm, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was the 21st date of their autumn British tour, with Mary Wells among the support acts, and the clip below is A Hard Day's Night.

events.headline: The Beatles ask the cheap seats to clap and the rich to rattle their jewellery
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Royal Variety Performance at the Prince of Wales Theatre in London on November 4, 1963, with the Queen Mother and Princess Margaret in the audience, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Before Twist and Shout, John Lennon asked the cheaper seats to clap and the rest of the house to rattle their jewellery, and the clip below is the studio Twist and Shout.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Star-Club in Hamburg
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Star-Club in Hamburg on November 4, 1962, the fourth date of a 14-night second residency that ran from November 1 to 14, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Love Me Do had come out a month earlier, and the clip below is that single.

events.headline: Bob Dylan gives his first solo concert at Carnegie Chapter Hall
events.summary_line_1: Bob Dylan played Carnegie Chapter Hall in New York on November 4, 1961, a concert promoted by Folklore Center owner Izzy Young, per the Gotham Center.
events.summary_line_2: Young recalled an audience of only 53, and the clip below is Song to Woody, from Dylan's debut album.

events.headline: Johnny Horton plays his last show at the Skyline Club
events.summary_line_1: Johnny Horton played the Skyline Club in Austin on November 4, 1960, the last show of his career, per Texas Escapes.
events.summary_line_2: He was killed in a car crash near Milano, Texas, after leaving the club, and the clip below is North to Alaska.
